scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

Alwa/Alodia is the kingdom; Soba is its capital and the focus of the cited excavations. Findings at specific Soba trenches are not generalized to every settlement or family across the imported outline. No other map ID is attached and no imported geometry or endpoints are rewritten.

The 2021 spatial paper opens with conquest in 1504 but makes clear that narrative histories were recorded much later, while its archaeological discussion shows abandonment and continued occupation at different places. The 2023 bead paper explicitly attributes 1504 to the late Funj Chronicle. Its statement that all discovered buildings were ruined in the thirteenth century is not made into a precisely dated universal abandonment. The 1530 imported endpoint is not used as a historical fall year. No exact successor-year geometry link has been certified, so fell remains null and successors empty.

The 2021 legacy paper was read for the project, ethnography, burial discussion, geophysical methods, buildings and production. Its inference from burial variety to religious or ethnic identities is not treated as proof. Its radiocarbon ranges around room feature 17 overlap awkwardly; the card describes the structural sequence without turning sample ranges into exact construction years. The lime-production item uses circa 1025 as a visible approximation for the first-quarter eleventh-century context, not an exact dated kiln firing.

The 2022 expedition report was downloaded as a 59-page PDF; pages 35 and 42 to 44 were closely read alongside searches for everyday-life topics. The report is preliminary. Its apparent February 2021/2022 processing typo and internally inconsistent aggregate grinding-tool totals are not repeated. Deposit 7 counts are used as reported, without turning morphology into chemical residue evidence. Plant specimens are not individually assigned to particular pots because the table does not establish those pairings. Grape seeds do not establish wine, local cultivation or a named recipe.

The 2024 isotope paper was read in accessible HTML for sample selection, dietary chemistry, results and interpretations. Fourteen human individuals were analyzed, not all twenty-three people in the cemetery. Tooth chemistry reflects enamel formation, not all adult meals. C4 is explained through relevant plants; maize is not projected into medieval Sudan. Milk and porridge are possible dietary interpretations, not directly recovered recipes. Geographic origins, religious affiliation and ethnic identity cannot be read unambiguously from these measurements. Seasonal mobility and accompanying families remain hypotheses, and animal baselines have limitations.

The two 2023 glass papers are separate studies. The bead paper analyzed twenty-three beads, mostly northern Indian glass groups, whereas the shard paper analyzed thirty fragments from vessels and windows. Glass-production regions, bead manufacture, trade routes and wearer identities are different questions. Mostly residual or mixed contexts do not give every item a precise use date. The cosmetic bottle is a catalogue identification, not proof of its contents, perfume recipe or a medical treatment. No local glass industry is asserted.

The 2023 expedition report was downloaded as a ten-page PDF and its text read. The December 2022 school events and early-2023 fieldwork are historical dated activities, not claims about schools operating today. Drawings are not neutral images of medieval life; teachers, textbooks and workshop discussion shaped them. Interviews on dress and homes cover Soba and Mahas, and the card does not collapse the two communities. The report notes recent migration into Soba; shared residence does not establish uninterrupted descent.

The project website supplies introductory identity and institutional context. Its exploratory aims are not presented as completed discoveries. Current changing measures of urban encroachment, estimated total area investigated, or claims about every class of resident are not used as a modern census.

No source reviewed here establishes a particular medieval Soba toilet or medical practice. Modern toilet construction mentioned in the reports is not projected backward to satisfy a topic quota. Humour concerns the effort of food preparation, never burials, conflict or people’s beliefs. No archaeological images, human remains photographs or identifiable children’s artwork are reproduced.

Dates on modern discoveries, reports and interviews refer to that work, not manufacture of medieval artifacts. Broad medieval house context remains undated rather than assigned a fictitious year. The narrative is author-checked and pending independent historical review; presence and schema validation do not certify all depth dimensions.

proposedOverrides.summary: Alwa was a medieval kingdom centred on Soba on the Blue Nile in present-day Sudan. Its capital housed royal and church institutions, workshops and communities connected to distant exchange networks.

identityEvidence.assessment: Outline around the central Sudanese Nile region is consistent with the intended Alwa/Alodia identity. This is a kingdom-level entry with evidence concentrated at Soba, not a card for all Sudan, all Nubian peoples or neighboring Makuria. Detailed boundaries and the imported 600 to 1530 coverage remain unverified.
